conn.p1: The app runs locally on both computers, but it may use the internet. That is how your two apps find each other – no server of your own, no account, no router settings:
conn.p1Group: The app runs locally on every computer, but it may use the internet. That is how your apps find each other – no server of your own, no account, no router settings:
conn.p2: Both apps announce themselves with your room code on public Nostr relays. The relays only introduce you – after that your apps talk directly (WebRTC, like a video call).
conn.p2Group: All apps announce themselves with your room code on public Nostr relays. The relays only introduce you – after that your apps talk directly (WebRTC, like a video call).
conn.p3: If a router blocks direct connections, data goes through a public MQTT server instead. It also keeps your latest state, so the others catch up even if you are not online at the same time.
conn.p4: Everything is encrypted with the key from your invite. Only tracker data travels – never ROMs or save files.

faq.a2a: It reads your game live – team, HP, levels, catches – but it never writes into the running game. That keeps your save safe.
faq.a2b: Between sessions it can edit your save file: dead Pokémon can be moved into PC box 18 (graveyard). This only works while the game is closed, and a backup is made first.
faq.a3: No. Everyone uses their own copy. The invite only contains settings, seeds and the room key; the randomizer rebuilds the identical game from your own ROM, and the app checks the checksum.
faq.a4: All main Pokémon games on Game Boy, Game Boy Color, Game Boy Advance and Nintendo DS (Gen 1–5) and their ROM hacks, plus X/Y to Ultra Sun/Ultra Moon on Nintendo 3DS (Gen 6–7). Live tracking works for the English and German releases; ROM hacks work when they keep the original memory layout.
faq.a5: Yes – choose them in the settings. mGBA streams live data through a small script you load once (Tools › Scripting). melonDS has no scripting, so it syncs after every in-game save.
faq.a6: Nothing gets lost. Each app keeps its own copy and both merge automatically when you’re connected again.
faq.a7: Right after it happens, save the diagnostics and send the file along with what you did. It holds what souldew read from the game and decided this session (song numbers, levels, what the turbo sound played) – no ROM, save file or invite.

guide.s2Nav: SoulLink › Host new SoulLink: pick a game (and optionally a hack), the number of players, a randomizer preset and the names. The app builds the games in seconds.

guide.s5: If a linked Pokémon faints, the pair dies for both of you automatically. The board, the graveyard and the log keep the score.

rules.autoDeath: A linked Pokémon that faints (live) kills the pair automatically

rules.b1: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area counts. Both catches of an area form a pair.
rules.b1Group: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area counts. All players’ catches on an area are linked into a group.
rules.b1Solo: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area may be caught. If it flees or faints, the area is used up.
rules.b2: If one Pokémon faints, its partner dies too – both go to the graveyard.
rules.b2Group: If one Pokémon faints, every Pokémon linked to it dies too – the whole group goes to the graveyard.
rules.b2Solo: A Pokémon that faints is dead – it goes to the graveyard and is never used again.
rules.b3: A pair is always in the team together or in the box together.
rules.b3Group: A group is always in the team together or in the box together.
rules.b4: If one of you blacks out, the run is over for both.
rules.b4Group: If one of you blacks out, the run is over for everyone.
rules.b4Solo: If your whole team faints (blackout), the run is over.
rules.b4SoloBox: The run is over once no living Pokémon is left – in the team or in the box.
rules.b4SoloOff: A blackout doesn’t end the run – you decide when it’s over.
rules.cheatsHint: From the play screen. Every use shows up in the log for both of you.
rules.cheatsHintGroup: From the play screen. Every use shows up in the log for all of you.
rules.discordHint: Optional: post catches and deaths to your Discord channel (Channel › Integrations › Webhook).
rules.discordLocal: Stays on this computer – your partner can add their own.
rules.discordLocalGroup: Stays on this computer – the others can add their own.
rules.dupesHint: Already own the evolution line? Keep looking.
rules.fail: A missed encounter costs the whole pair
rules.failGroup: A missed encounter costs the whole group
rules.hostOnly: Only the host can change this.
rules.shiny: Shiny clause: shinies may always be caught and stay unlinked
rules.typeHelpHint: In battle: how your moves land, what hits you and each Pokémon’s weaknesses. Off hides it for every player.

rules.typeHint: Primary types may not repeat in the team.
runs.deleteText: This removes the run from this computer: the games built for it, the save files, the board with all encounters and deaths, and the invite.
runs.deleteTrash: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand. Your partner’s copy is not affected.
runs.deleteTrashGroup: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand. The copies of the other players are not affected.
runs.deleteTrashSolo: The folder is moved to the trash folder inside the app data (runs/.trash) – you can restore it by hand.

runs.host3Link: Give the others the 6-digit invite code

runs.solo3: The app builds your game – start playing
runs.soloRule1: Only the first Pokémon you meet in each area counts.
runs.soloRule2: Fainted means dead – it goes to the graveyard.

session.centerHint: Pokémon Center visits since the last badge – count them yourself.
session.rulesHint: Change the run rules without leaving the game
set.coffeePop: Coffee hint on legendary encounters in stream overlays
set.coffeePopHint: Now and then a cheeky toast about the legendary pops up in your Alerts overlay, with the coffee link.
set.controlsText: Keyboard keys for the built-in emulator. Click a key, then press the new one. Changes apply the next time a game starts.
set.emuText: The built-in emulator works for every system up to the DS and has the best live sync. Nintendo 3DS games run in Azahar. External emulators are optional otherwise.
set.fullTurbo: Full-power turbo: no brake while fast-forwarding
set.fullTurboHint: The game may use almost all of the computer’s time while fast-forwarding, and DS games skip drawing frames nobody sees. Never steps down. If the app reacts sluggishly while fast-forwarding, turn it off. Normal speed stays the same.
set.gpuFallbackCrash: The graphics backend {backend} kept crashing. souldew uses “Automatic” again from the next start – you can change it in Settings.
set.gpuFallbackStart: souldew didn’t open with the graphics backend {backend}, so it uses “Automatic” again. You can change it in Settings.
set.gpuHint: If the game stutters or the sound crackles, try Vulkan. Automatic lets the system decide.
set.gpuRestart: The new graphics backend is used after a restart of souldew.
set.legal: Pokémon and all related names are trademarks of Nintendo, Game Freak and The Pokémon Company. souldew is a fan project and does not include or download games.
set.libraryText: Games you add are copied into the library folder. You can also include folders where your ROMs already are.
set.mgbaScriptAgain: For live data with mGBA: Tools › Scripting… › File › Load script… and pick this file (again after every mGBA restart):
set.nag: Show the joke license window now and then
set.nagHint: A parody of old shareware nag screens. souldew stays free either way.
set.name: Your name
set.native: Fast player for DS, GBA and Game Boy
set.nativeHint: Runs the game with the real emulators (melonDS, mGBA, Gambatte) directly on your computer: full speed even on weaker PCs, and fast-forward that really reaches 4× and more. Live sync, cheats, save states and the in-game save work as before. Save states from the other player can’t be loaded here (and the other way round). Off: the browser emulator as before. Applies to the next game you start.
set.shareScreenAll: Share my screen with the other players
set.shareScreenHint: While you play, the others see your game small in a corner. It is only sent while someone is watching.
set.soundsAll: Sounds on this computer (start-up chime, catches, deaths, badges, pings)
set.speedGuard: Step down when the computer can’t keep up
set.speedGuardHint: Off: the speed you pick stays as it is, the bar shows when a scene runs slower. On: a level that isn’t reached for a few seconds drops to the highest one that holds.
set.themeText: Colour scheme of the whole app. The colour-blind schemes replace the green/red signals (alive, dead, warnings) with colours that stay apart with that colour vision.
set.turboMax: Turbo step “Max”: as fast as this computer can
set.turboMaxHint: After 4× comes “Max” – no speed limit at all. How fast it gets depends on the game and the computer.
solo.overCapN: {n} Pokémon over the cap – box them before the boss.|{n} Pokémon over the cap – box them before the boss.

spoiler.otherDeviceName: This game was built on {name}’s computer – no spoiler data here.
spoiler.streamerText: Your viewers would see what the randomizer rolled. Switch streamer mode off on the Stream page to look.
spoiler.text: Wild Pokémon per route and the starters. Once you look, you no longer play blind.
spoiler.title: What the randomizer rolled
states.autoTitle: Automatic – taken while you play and when you close the game
states.full: All 8 slots are used – overwrite or delete one
states.keysHint: F5 saves to the selected slot, F8 loads it.
states.lastSavedBefore: Last saved in-game: before this session
states.listFailed: Couldn’t read the save states. Try again in a moment.
states.loadConfirm: Load “{name}”? Progress since then is lost.
states.openHint: All save states – load, overwrite, delete
states.otherCore: Made with another emulator core – can’t be loaded here
states.title: Save states
states.unsavedHint: progress since then isn’t saved in the game yet
stats.levelsGained: +{n} level since the catch|+{n} levels since the catch
stats.noSurvivor: Shows up once a catch has gained levels.
stats.segmentsHint: Counted on the way to each boss – where the run hurts most.
steps.catchText: Catch the first Pokémon of an area – it’s filed by itself and your partner’s catch there becomes its pair.
steps.catchTextGroup: Catch the first Pokémon of an area – it’s filed by itself and the others’ catches there join its group.
steps.catchTextSolo: Catch the first Pokémon of an area – it’s filed by itself. Only the first encounter of each area counts.
steps.partnerInvite: Create a code and tell it to {name} – their app joins once you allow it. You can play already, everything is merged later.
steps.partnerWaitJoin: {name} hosts this run – as soon as their app is open, you’re connected. Meanwhile you can already play.
steps.playText: Start your game – your team appears here live as soon as you have Pokémon.
steps.playersInvite: Create a code for each player and tell it to them – their app joins once you allow it. You can play already, everything is merged later.
steps.title: Next step
steps.waitOthers: Still missing: {names} – they join with their own invite code. Meanwhile you can already play.
stream.api: Open API – build your own layout
stream.apiLocal: Pages on this computer without a token, too: layouts opened from disk in a browser and other local web servers (localhost)
stream.apiOpenObs: Without a token, OBS (also local files), scripts and souldew may read – other websites can’t.
stream.apiSafe: Read-only and on this computer only (127.0.0.1): no ROMs, saves, file names, invite codes or spoilers. Run: {name}
stream.apiText: Want your own design instead of souldew’s? Your browser sources can read the run as JSON – teams, links, graveyard, encounters, locations – get every catch, death and level-up live, and load the same sprites the app shows.
stream.dragHint: Drag into OBS: it becomes a browser source of the right size
stream.followOff: These links always show “{name}”, even when you play another run. Pick “Current run” for links that keep working from run to run.
stream.followOn: The links follow the run you play: start a new run or open another one and the overlays switch by themselves – OBS keeps the same sources. Now: {name}
stream.inObsHint: An overlay with this widget is open outside the app – in OBS or a browser.
stream.modeOff: Switch it on before you go live – souldew then covers what your viewers mustn’t see.
stream.modeOn: souldew is safe to show: everything below is covered on every page until you switch it off.
stream.noRunText: The overlays show a run live. Start a SoulLink or a Nuzlocke first.
stream.obsCount: one overlay live in OBS|{count} overlays live in OBS
stream.onAirHint: Streamer mode is on – codes, keys, paths and spoilers are covered
stream.plBusy: Port {port} is taken – is Pokélink itself open? Close it or pick another port.
stream.plLocal: Also themes from another web server on this computer (localhost, any port) – themes opened from disk or from Pokélink’s website work without it
stream.plNote: Instead of the name, user=p1 … p4 works too. Themes show what Pokélink’s data has: team, levels, HP, status, items, moves and badges.
stream.plOffHint: Off – nothing listens until you switch it on.
stream.plText: Already have a Pokélink theme you like? souldew can feed it: switch the bridge on, then open the theme with one of the endings below instead of its own ?user=… – in OBS just like before.
stream.s1: Pick a widget and set it up – the preview is exactly what OBS shows, live.
stream.s2: Drag “Drag into OBS” onto your scene – OBS makes a browser source of the right size. Or copy the URL into a new browser source.
stream.s3: Keep souldew open while you stream: the overlays update the moment something happens.
stream.testNoObs: It shows in the preview. No alert overlay is open in OBS yet – add the Alerts widget there.
stream.testObs: It shows in the preview and in one overlay outside the app.|It shows in the preview and in {count} overlays outside the app.
stream.wAlertsText: Deaths, catches, badges, evolutions and every 10th level pop up for a few seconds – with sound if you like.
stream.wCardText: One player’s team in detail: nicknames, levels, HP, status, badges and play time.
stream.wCountersText: Alive, in the graveyard, caught and badges – the numbers pop when they change.
stream.wStatsText: Run name, play time, badges and the counts in one slim line – for the bottom of the screen.
stream.wTeamText: Every team side by side – one column per linked group, with level, HP and status. Dead groups turn grey.
stream.wWhereText: The route or town each player is in right now, and the battle they are fighting.
team.empty: Your team shows up here as soon as you have Pokémon.
team.untrackedHint: Not filed to an area yet – see the inbox on the board.
theme.contrastHint: Black background, brighter text and edges
theme.deutanHint: For deuteranopia / protanopia: blue and orange instead of green and red
theme.tritanHint: For tritanopia: teal and magenta instead of blue and yellow
trophy.backfillText: Your past runs already earned {n} achievement – have a look under Trophies.|Your past runs already earned {n} achievements – have a look under Trophies.
trophy.secretText: Keep playing – you’ll know it when it happens.
trophy.title: Trophies
unsaved.never: You haven’t saved in the game yet.
unsaved.sinceSession: You haven’t saved in the game since you started playing.
unsaved.text: A save state of where you left off is kept, but only an in-game save is safe – save in the game menu first.
unsaved.title: Not saved in the game yet
upd.availableSide: Version {version} is available – see the sidebar.
upd.badSignature: The update could not be verified: its signature is missing or wrong, so it was not downloaded. Your installed version is unchanged.
upd.browser: Updates are installed by the desktop app.
upd.dataSafe: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in your Library folder, not inside the app.
upd.dataSafeLinux: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in ~/.config/SoulLink Studio, not inside the app.
upd.dataSafeWin: Your runs, saves and settings are kept: they live in your user folder (AppData), not inside the app.
upd.gatekeeper: If macOS says it can’t check the app for malicious software, right-click it in Applications › Open › Open. That is needed once because souldew is not notarized by Apple.
upd.laterHint: The update is installed when you quit the app.
upd.manual2: In the Finder window that opened, drag souldew onto Applications and choose “Replace”.
upd.manual2Linux: In the folder that opened is {file}, already executable. Replace your old souldew AppImage with it – under the old file name if a Steam or desktop shortcut points to it.
upd.manual2Win: In the Explorer window that opened, double-click {file}. It installs the new version and keeps your data.
upd.manualText: Version {version} is downloaded and checked. Replace the app by hand to finish.
upd.manualTextWin: Version {version} is downloaded and checked. Run the installer to finish.
upd.noRelease: No update has been published yet.
upd.notConfigured: Updates are not set up for this build.
upd.readyText: Restart to use version {version}. Your runs, saves and settings stay as they are.
upd.readyTextWin: Restart to install version {version} – it takes a few seconds, then souldew opens again. Your runs, saves and settings stay as they are.
upd.reasonBlocked: macOS did not let the app replace itself. You can allow it under System Settings › Privacy & Security › App Management, or replace it by hand.
upd.reasonDmg: The app is running from the disk image instead of from Applications.
upd.reasonLaunch: The installer could not be started automatically.
upd.reasonMinVersion: Your version is too old to update automatically.
upd.reasonPortable: This copy of souldew wasn’t installed with the installer (it runs from an unpacked folder), so it can’t update itself.
upd.reasonReadOnly: Your user account can’t write to the folder the app is in.
upd.reasonSignature: The new version’s signature could not be verified, so it was not installed automatically.
upd.reasonTranslocated: The app was opened straight from the download instead of from Applications.
upd.saveFirst: Save in the game first – restarting closes it.
upd.smartscreen: If Windows SmartScreen says it protected your PC, click “More info” › “Run anyway”. That is needed because souldew is not signed with a paid certificate.
upd.stepLaunch: Starting the installer – souldew closes and opens again by itself
